title: Winter is Kolkata's most polluted season
text: Average PM2.5 in winter was 99.3 µg/m³, approximately 4.1× higher than monsoon (24.4 µg/m³).

title: January peaks while July clears the air
text: January recorded the highest average concentration (115.3 µg/m³), whereas July saw the lowest (13.9 µg/m³).

title: 58% of days had acceptable air quality
text: Across the observation window, 58.2% of days met Good or Satisfactory levels, while 22.7% experienced Poor to Severe air.

title: 42% of days exceeded the CPCB 24-hr threshold
text: 356 of 852 recorded days (41.8%) surpassed India's National Ambient Air Quality standard of 60 µg/m³.

title: Weekend air quality comparison
text: No statistically significant difference between weekdays (59.1 µg/m³) and weekends (60.4 µg/m³, p=0.69).

title: Atmospheric ventilation disperses pollution
text: Holding other factors fixed, each +1 km/h increase in wind speed is associated with a 2.68 µg/m³ decrease in daily PM2.5 (p < 0.001).

title: Thermal inversions trap particulate matter in cool weather
text: Holding other factors constant, cooler ambient temperatures are associated with elevated PM2.5 concentrations (slope -3.96 µg/m³ per °C, p < 0.001).

title: Wet deposition cleans the atmosphere
text: Days with precipitation (>2.5 mm) averaged 28.4 µg/m³ PM2.5 compared to 76.7 µg/m³ on dry days.

title: Model accurately captures macroscopic seasonal variations
text: The headline regression model achieves an R² of 0.76 and RMSE of 23.1 µg/m³ on unseen chronological test data (47% exact category accuracy).

title: Post-monsoon exhibits the highest prediction uncertainty
text: Prediction error is highest during post-monsoon (MAE 23.4 µg/m³), where boundary layer dynamics and sporadic episodic events create sharp non-linear swings.

title: Historical maximum reached 245.8 µg/m³
text: The highest observed 24-hr concentration occurred on 2023-01-22 (245.8 µg/m³, Category: Very poor).

title: Longest consecutive pollution episode lasted 24 days
text: The city experienced a stretch of 24 consecutive days with air quality categorized as Poor, Very Poor, or Severe (ending 2023-02-01).

title: 852 verified daily observations analyzed
text: All calculations utilize real meteorological reanalysis and atmospheric sensor records for Kolkata (Coordinates: 22.57°N, 88.36°E) without data fabrication.
